hook.1: Welcome to the learning centre. Let's compare fictional choices, not buy anything.
hook.2: A higher possible return is not a promise. Check risk, access to your money and when you need it.
hook.3: Spreading money across different investments can reduce concentration risk, but cannot remove all risk.

lesson.title: A range is not a promise
lesson.prompt: Move the time slider. Assumption: ₹10,000, a 6% annual model rate with a 2 percentage-point spread, 4% annual inflation and annual compounding for up to 8 years. This toy range excludes losses, fees and taxes: real investments can lose money and fall outside it. What does it show?
lesson.hint1: Past performance does not guarantee future returns.
lesson.hint2: Choose the answer that treats the graph as an illustration, not a promise.
lesson.explanation: The graph uses assumptions, not a forecast or a minimum return. Investments can lose money; a longer horizon does not guarantee success.
lesson.promise: The graph promises that my money cannot fall below its lower line.
lesson.assumption: It illustrates assumed growth; neither the return nor the lower line is guaranteed.

compare.assumption: Assumption: fictional educational cards only. No quoted market rates, fees or taxes; no real provider or product. The answer tests the stated scenario, not what you should buy.
compare.hint1: First match the goal, time horizon, risk tolerance and access needs. A higher possible return is not enough.
compare.hint2: One company is not diversification. A diversified portfolio can still lose value.

fd.risk: Risk: a fixed deposit is a term deposit, not stock-market ownership. Lower market-price risk does not mean every financial risk disappears.
fd.liquidity: Access: early withdrawal can reduce interest or carry a penalty; check the terms.
fd.horizon: Horizon: match the deposit's maturity date to the date you need the money.

bonds.risk: Risk: a bond lends to an issuer. Default and interest-rate changes can cause losses; a fixed coupon does not fix its resale price.
bonds.liquidity: Access: selling before maturity needs a buyer and can mean selling at a loss.
bonds.horizon: Horizon: consider maturity and whether you can hold the bond until then.

mutualFunds.risk: Risk: mutual funds pool investors' money into securities. Risk depends on the holdings; a diversified equity fund is not a guaranteed-return deposit.
mutualFunds.liquidity: Access: check the fund's redemption terms, settlement time and any lock-in or exit charge.
mutualFunds.horizon: Horizon: for equity exposure, consider a longer horizon and ability to bear losses, not money needed soon.

equities.risk: Risk: equities are company ownership. Prices can fall; holding only one company concentrates risk.
equities.liquidity: Access: converting shares into cash depends on selling at the available market price; liquidity is not price safety.
equities.horizon: Horizon: volatile equity prices can be unsuitable for money needed soon, even if shares can be sold.

decision.title: Check a long-horizon statement
decision.prompt: Fictional Mira has a flexible project goal in 8 years, separate emergency savings and can accept losses. She is learning about pooled, diversified equity exposure. Which statement describes that approach without a false promise? This is not a product recommendation.
decision.fd: FD: guarantees the highest growth for every long-term goal
decision.bonds: Bonds: a fixed coupon guarantees the resale price
decision.mutualFunds: Mutual funds: diversified equity holdings, with no guaranteed return
decision.equities: Equities: owning one company's shares removes concentration risk
decision.explanation: For this question, pooled diversified equity holdings describe the stated approach. Neither a fixed coupon nor diversification guarantees gains; one company's shares are not diversification. Other goals may call for a different approach.

consequence.range: Assumption, not a forecast: starting with ₹10,000, annual compounding for 8 years at assumed rates of 4% and 8% gives ₹13,685.69 and ₹18,509.30 respectively, before fees and taxes. These are model endpoints, not promised outcomes or bounds on losses.
consequence.explanation: You compared risk and access, not just a return number. Actual investment outcomes may be lower, including a loss. Diversification reduces concentration risk, not every risk; match your horizon and needs.

books.title: A different goal: next term's books
books.prompt: Fictional Tara needs the full book budget in 3 months and cannot accept a market loss. Assumption: the fictional low-risk FD matures before payment and its withdrawal terms are suitable; the bond matures in 5 years with no assured early buyer; the fund and shares can fall in value. Which card fits these stated constraints?
books.fd: FD: lower-risk deposit maturing before the book payment
books.bonds: Bonds: wait for a buyer before the book payment
books.mutualFunds: Mutual funds: use volatile equity holdings for the book payment
books.equities: Equities: hope one company's shares rise before the book payment
books.explanation: The assumed deposit terms fit this near-term payment better than volatile or hard-to-sell assets. Check actual maturity and withdrawal conditions; this fictional answer is not a recommendation.

course.title: A different goal: a course fee
course.prompt: Fictional Arun must pay a course fee in 6 months, needs the whole amount and cannot absorb losses. Assumption: the fictional low-risk FD matures before the fee is due with suitable withdrawal terms; the bond matures in 5 years with no assured early buyer; equity funds and shares may fall. Which card fits this goal?
course.fd: FD: lower-risk deposit with a matching maturity date
course.bonds: Bonds: depend on selling an illiquid bond early
course.mutualFunds: Mutual funds: depend on short-term equity gains
course.equities: Equities: put the full fee into one company's shares
course.explanation: For money needed soon without room for losses, access and capital preservation matter. The assumed deposit matches this scenario; real terms must still be checked, and this is not a product recommendation.

guaranteed_return.review: Your choice: treated growth or a fixed coupon as a promise. Safer choice: distinguish an assumed return from an assured outcome and check risks. Concept: return and resale value are not guaranteed. Why it matters: a loss can leave a goal unfunded.

ignored_horizon.review: Your choice: relied on volatile prices or an early buyer for money needed soon. Safer choice: match maturity, access and risk to the payment date. Concept: liquidity and time horizon. Why it matters: you may have to sell at a loss or miss the payment.

concentrated_risk.review: Your choice: treated one company's shares as diversification. Safer choice: recognise a portfolio spread across different investments. Concept: diversification reduces concentration risk but does not eliminate losses. Why it matters: a single company's setback can hit all the money placed in it.
